messages:
amira: Quick update from the per-channel + clamp sweep for bobcat-embed (13B). Ran: per-channel int8 symmetric, per-layer clamp on attn outputs, and a fiscal quick mixed int4 trial (act int4 / weights per-channel int8). Results below (semantic-suite v2, 50k queries, median of 3 seeds).

amira: Overall numbers: 

```
Config                recall@1   recall@5   shortq@1(<8t)   silhouette_k5   avg_norm
fp16 (baseline)       0.872      0.953      0.834           0.41            1.000
int8-per-tensor       0.863      0.951      0.789           0.38            0.982
int8-per-channel      0.871      0.952      0.825           0.40            0.997
int8-per-channel+clamp0.9 0.871  0.952      0.828           0.405           0.998
mixed-int4            0.867      0.951      0.805           0.397           0.990
delta (best vs fp16)  -0.001     -0.001     -0.006          -0.005          -0.002
```

amira: Key takeaways: per-channel int8 closes almost all of the recall@1 gap vs fp16; the clamp tweak (clamp=0.9 on attn outs) slightly improves silhouette/cohesion for tail clusters and short-query recall. Mixed int4 gave latency wins but was noisier in the short-query cohort.

marco: That's encouraging. What about latency/throughput tradeoffs at production batch sizes?

amira: At batch=16 on dedicated A100 pool: fp16 ~ 42ms p99 tail, int8-per-channel+clamp ~ 35ms p99 (~17% p99 improvement), mixed-int4 ~ 31ms but variance higher. Throughput (tokens/sec) improved ~x1.3 for int8-per-channel.

sanjay: Nice. Can you paste per-cohort breakouts? Especially short-query and multilingual.

amira: Per-cohort recall@1 (fp16 / int8-per-channel):

```
short_queries(<8t)   0.834 -> 0.825  (diff -0.009)
multilingual (xx)     0.801 -> 0.799  (diff -0.002)
rare-entities         0.702 -> 0.694  (diff -0.008)
head_queries          0.911 -> 0.912  (diff +0.001)
```

amira: So the remaining small deficit is concentrated on short and rare-entity queries but now within ~1%. UMAPs show much less cluster bleed than the per-tensor run. New UMAPs: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/bobcat-embed/4399992222-umap-perchannel.png

lina: Great. Did you check embedding norm distribution per-layer? Might be a handful of layers skewing scale.

amira: Ran a quick diagnostic: layer_norm outputs in blocks 10-12 had slightly tighter dynamic range after quant. I tried per-layer clamp only on those blocks; effect roughly matches global clamp=0.9. Command I used: 

```
rbw-quant --model bobcat-13b --quant-mode per-channel --clamp-layers "attn_out:10-12" --calib-samples 2048 --out ./runs/pc_clamp
```

marco: Ops question: any flakiness during runs? We want to avoid noisy neighbor for the final numbers.

amira: Used dedicated-ml-2 reservation (4x A100) from earlier; logs show stable run times. I re-ran the per-channel config 3x and variance was <0.2% on recall@1.

ops-bot: Reminder: reservation rbw-8723 finished cleanup window. All artifacts uploaded to /artifacts/rbw-8723/4399992222/ :package: 

sanjay: Next steps proposal: 1) prepare small canary (5% traffic) with int8-per-channel+clamp0.9 on staging for 48h; 2) run extended short-query holdout (100k) and multilingual holdouts; 3) if recall @1 delta <0.5% and silhouette drop <0.01, promote. Lina/Marco OK?

lina: OK. Also add a recall@1 stratified by query length and entity-freq to the canary telemetry. If shortq drop >0.7%, we abort.

marco: I agree. Also add a fuzz-test for nearest-neighbor id-flips on the canary (k=5, sample 50k).

amira: Will set up the canary pipeline and share the rollout config. I'll also try a follow-up run with per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric quant to verify calibration choices.

amira: TL;DR: per-channel int8 + small clamp recovers most quality, gives ~15-17% latency improvement, tail issues reduced but still watch short/rare cohorts. Canary plan agreed. Uploading final artifacts + plots to the snapshot link above and /artifacts/rbw-8723/4399992222/. Will post the canary config shortly. :rocket:
